# EU AI Act Compliance Requirements for High-Risk AI Hiring Tools: Current Status and Enforcement Analysis

## Executive Summary

The EU AI Act establishes comprehensive compliance requirements for companies deploying high-risk AI hiring tools, with full obligations taking effect on August 2, 2026. AI systems used for recruitment, selection, and hiring decisions are explicitly classified as high-risk under Annex III of the Act. Companies must implement extensive technical, organizational, and governance measures including conformity assessments, human oversight protocols, bias testing, and transparency disclosures. Violations can result in substantial fines up to €35 million or 7% of annual worldwide turnover for the most serious infractions. However, no enforcement actions have been taken yet, and several implementation details remain unclear.

## Key Findings

### Classification and Scope Requirements

**High-Risk Classification** (Confidence: 85%)
AI systems used for recruitment, selection, and hiring decisions are classified as high-risk under Annex III of the EU AI Act. [What the EU AI Act Means for Staffing Businesses](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/what-the-act-means-for-staffing-businesses/), [What Does the EU AI Act Mean for Employers?](https://www.cliffordchance.com/content/dam/cliffordchance/briefings/2024/08/what-does-the-eu-ai-act-mean-for-employers.pdf), [AI in Recruitment Processes: Navigating High-risk Systems for AI Deployers](https://www.legalnodes.com/article/ai-in-recruitment-processes-navigating-high-risk-systems-for-ai-deployers)

**Extraterritorial Application** (Confidence: 75%)
The EU AI Act applies extraterritorially to companies outside the EU whose AI systems are used or have effects within the European Union. [What is the EU AI Act? Employer compliance guide](https://boundlesshq.com/blog/what-is-the-eu-ai-act-everything-you-need-to-know/), [EU AI Act: Application timeline and implications](https://www.toprankedlegal.com/eu-ai-act-application-timeline-and-implications/)

### Pre-Market Requirements

**Conformity Assessment** (Confidence: 75%)
High-risk AI hiring tools require mandatory conformity assessment before market entry. [AI Risk Classification: Guide to EU AI Act Risk Categories](https://gdprlocal.com/ai-risk-classification/), [AI Act: high-risk AI systems – what applies, what is due when?](https://naaia.ai/ai-act-high-risk/)

**EU Database Registration** (Confidence: 65%)
Companies must register high-risk AI systems in the EU Database. [AI Risk Classification: Guide to EU AI Act Risk Categories](https://gdprlocal.com/ai-risk-classification/)

**Technical Documentation** (Confidence: 75%)
Extensive technical documentation is required for high-risk AI hiring systems. [AI Risk Classification: Guide to EU AI Act Risk Categories](https://gdprlocal.com/ai-risk-classification/), [What the EU AI Act Means for Staffing Businesses](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/what-the-act-means-for-staffing-businesses/)

### Operational Compliance Requirements

**Quality Management System** (Confidence: 70%)
Providers must implement and maintain a quality management system for high-risk AI systems. [EU AI Act – What are the obligations for "high-risk AI systems"?](https://www.aoshearman.com/en/insights/ao-shearman-on-tech/zooming-in-on-ai-10-eu-ai-act-what-are-the-obligations-for-high-risk-ai-systems)

**Risk Management System** (Confidence: 70%)
Deployers must implement and document a risk management system as a continuous iterative process. [EU AI Act – What are the obligations for "high-risk AI systems"?](https://www.aoshearman.com/en/insights/ao-shearman-on-tech/zooming-in-on-ai-10-eu-ai-act-what-are-the-obligations-for-high-risk-ai-systems)

**Human Oversight Protocols** (Confidence: 85%)
Deployers must implement human oversight protocols for high-risk AI hiring systems. [AI Risk Classification: Guide to EU AI Act Risk Categories](https://gdprlocal.com/ai-risk-classification/), [What the EU AI Act Means for Staffing Businesses](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/what-the-act-means-for-staffing-businesses/), [Artificial Intelligence and Human Resources in the EU](https://www.crowell.com/en/insights/client-alerts/artificial-intelligence-and-human-resources-in-the-eu-a-2026-legal-overview)

**Bias Testing** (Confidence: 75%)
Companies must conduct mandatory bias testing for high-risk AI hiring tools. [What the EU AI Act Means for Staffing Businesses](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/what-the-act-means-for-staffing-businesses/), [How the EU AI Act Changes Recruitment - What Employers Need to Know](https://www.heymilo.ai/blog/how-the-eu-ai-act-changes-recruitment-and-what-employers-need-to-know)

**Transparency Disclosures** (Confidence: 85%)
Transparency disclosures to candidates are required when AI is used in hiring processes. [What the EU AI Act Means for Staffing Businesses](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/what-the-act-means-for-staffing-businesses/), [How the EU AI Act Changes Recruitment - What Employers Need to Know](https://www.heymilo.ai/blog/how-the-eu-ai-act-changes-recruitment-and-what-employers-need-to-know), [The EU Artificial Intelligence Act and Talent Management](https://www.edge-cert.org/article/eu-artificial-intelligence-act-and-talent-management/)

**Continuous Monitoring** (Confidence: 70%)
Continuous monitoring of high-risk AI hiring systems is required. [What the EU AI Act Means for Staffing Businesses](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/what-the-act-means-for-staffing-businesses/)

### Implementation Timeline

**Act Entry into Force** (Confidence: 95%)
The EU AI Act entered into force on August 1, 2024. [Implementation Timeline | EU Artificial Intelligence Act](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline/), [AI Act | Shaping Europe's digital future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)

**High-Risk System Obligations** (Confidence: 90%)
High-risk AI system obligations become applicable on August 2, 2026. [What the EU AI Act Means for Staffing Businesses](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/what-the-act-means-for-staffing-businesses/), [The Impact of the EU AI Act on Human Resources Activities](https://www.hunton.com/insights/legal/the-impact-of-the-eu-ai-act-on-human-resources-activities), [Timeline for the Implementation of the EU AI Act](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)

### Penalties and Enforcement

**Maximum Penalties for Prohibited Practices** (Confidence: 90%)
Violations of prohibited AI practices can result in fines up to €35 million or 7% of annual worldwide turnover, whichever is higher. [Article 99: Penalties | EU Artificial Intelligence Act](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/99/), [Penalties of the EU AI Act: The High Cost of Non-Compliance](https://www.holisticai.com/blog/penalties-of-the-eu-ai-act)

**Other Violations Penalties** (Confidence: 85%)
Other violations of the AI Act can result in fines up to €20 million or 4% of annual worldwide turnover, whichever is higher. [Fines under the AI Act - A bottomless pit?](https://www.taylorwessing.com/en/interface/2021/ai-act/fines-under-the-ai-act---a-bottomless-pit), [Article 99: Penalties | EU Artificial Intelligence Act](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/99/)

**Current Enforcement Status** (Confidence: 80%)
No specific enforcement actions have been taken yet under the EU AI Act for high-risk AI hiring tools.

## Contradictions & Uncertainties

### Timeline Discrepancies
There is conflicting information about the exact compliance dates for high-risk AI systems. While most sources indicate August 2, 2026, some suggest potential delays to December 2, 2027 for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III and August 2, 2028 for systems covered by Annex I. [Timeline for the Implementation of the EU AI Act](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act) vs. [When will EU AI Act high-risk AI compliance become applicable?](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)

### Penalty Amount Conflicts
There are conflicting penalty amounts cited for non-prohibited AI Act violations, with sources citing both €20 million/4% and €15 million/3% of turnover. [Fines under the AI Act - A bottomless pit?](https://www.taylorwessing.com/en/interface/2021/ai-act/fines-under-the-ai-act---a-bottomless-pit) vs. [Article 99: Penalties | EU Artificial Intelligence Act](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/99/)

## Knowledge Gaps

1. **Technical Standards Uncertainty**: Specific technical standards and conformity assessment procedures for AI hiring systems remain unclear
2. **Scope Ambiguity**: The precise scope of 'work-related contractual relationships' and which specific HR AI tools qualify as high-risk needs clarification
3. **GDPR Interaction**: The interaction between EU AI Act requirements and existing GDPR obligations for AI hiring systems requires further guidance
4. **Enforcement Precedents**: No concrete enforcement actions or case studies are available yet for high-risk AI hiring tools
5. **Implementation Guidance**: Detailed implementation guidance from regulatory authorities is still pending

report:
# Comparative Analysis: EU AI Act Foundation Model Requirements vs. US Federal AI Policy

## Executive Summary

This report compares the European Union's AI Act requirements for foundation model providers with current United States federal AI policy approaches. The analysis reveals a stark contrast between the EU's comprehensive, mandatory regulatory framework and the US's evolving policy landscape characterized by voluntary guidance and recent policy shifts. The EU AI Act establishes specific obligations for General-Purpose AI (GPAI) model providers, including transparency requirements and systemic risk thresholds, while the US currently relies primarily on voluntary frameworks following the revocation of Executive Order 14110 in January 2025.

## Key Findings

### Regulatory Framework Structure

**EU Approach: Mandatory Legal Requirements**
- The EU AI Act establishes binding legal obligations for GPAI model providers, including requirements to create technical documentation, training data summaries, and copyright policies as transparency obligations (confidence: 0.85) [[High-level summary of the AI Act](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/high-level-summary/), [The regulation of foundation models in the EU AI Act](https://www.ibanet.org/the-regulation-of-foundation-models-in-the-eu-ai-act)]
- GPAI model obligations under the EU AI Act became applicable on August 2, 2025 (confidence: 0.68) [[Foundation Models under the EU AI Act - Stanford CRFM](https://crfm.stanford.edu/2024/08/01/eu-ai-act.html)]

**US Approach: Voluntary Guidance Framework**
- The NIST AI Risk Management Framework provides voluntary guidance rather than mandatory requirements (confidence: 0.36) [[NIST AI Risk Management Framework](https://www.diligent.com/resources/blog/nist-ai-risk-management-framework), [NIST vs ISO - Compare AI Frameworks](https://www.modelop.com/ai-governance/ai-regulations-standards/nist-vs-iso)]
- US Executive Order 14110 on AI was revoked by the Trump administration in January 2025 (confidence: 0.60) [[Trump Administration Early Executive Orders Signal Shift in AI Policy](https://www.kslaw.com/news-and-insights/trump-administration-early-executive-orders-signal-shift-in-ai-policy)]

### Risk Thresholds and Model Classification

| Aspect | EU AI Act | US Federal Policy |
|--------|-----------|-------------------|
| **Risk Threshold** | GPAI models with systemic risk defined as those using more than 10^25 FLOPs for training | No specific computational thresholds established |
| **Model Categories** | Clear distinction between standard GPAI models and systemic risk models | No formal model classification system |
| **Applicability** | Mandatory for all qualifying models | Voluntary compliance frameworks |

The EU establishes a clear computational threshold where GPAI models with systemic risk are defined as those using more than 10^25 FLOPs for training (confidence: 0.85) [[High-level summary of the AI Act](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/high-level-summary/), [Comparing EU and U.S. State Laws on AI](https://www.dataversity.net/articles/comparing-eu-and-u-s-state-laws-on-ai-a-checklist-for-proactive-compliance/)].

### Enforcement Mechanisms

**EU Enforcement Structure**
- EU AI Act violations can result in fines up to EUR 35 million or 7% of worldwide annual turnover (confidence: 0.42) [[What is AI Governance? | IBM](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/ai-governance), [The EU AI Act: Oversight and Enforcement](https://www.orrick.com/en/Insights/2024/09/The-EU-AI-Act-Oversight-and-Enforcement)]
- Enforcement is split between the EU AI Office for GPAI models and national authorities for other AI systems (confidence: 0.36) [[EU AI Act: Timeline, Enforcement & Fines](https://www.spektr.com/blog/eu-ai-act-timeline-enforcement-fines-and-how-to-prepare)]

**US Enforcement Approach**
- Currently lacks federal enforcement mechanisms for foundation models
- The Trump administration's National Policy Framework calls for federal preemption of state AI laws (confidence: 0.68) [[National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/03.20.26-National-Policy-Framework-for-Artificial-Intelligence-Legislative-Recommendations.pdf), [The White House Legislative Recommendations](https://www.ropesgray.com/en/insights/alerts/2026/03/the-white-house-legislative-recommendations-national-policy-framework-for-artificial-intelligence-an)]

### Compliance Requirements Comparison

| Requirement Type | EU AI Act | US Federal Policy |
|------------------|-----------|-------------------|
| **Technical Documentation** | Mandatory for all GPAI providers | Voluntary under NIST framework |
| **Training Data Summaries** | Required transparency obligation | No federal requirement |
| **Copyright Policies** | Mandatory disclosure | No federal requirement |
| **Risk Assessment** | Required for systemic risk models | Voluntary guidance available |
| **Incident Reporting** | Mandatory for qualifying models | No federal mandate |

## Contradictions & Uncertainties

### Policy Continuity Issues
A significant contradiction exists regarding US federal AI policy continuity. While some sources reference Executive Order 14110 as current policy, other sources confirm its revocation by the Trump administration in January 2025 [[Trump Administration Early Executive Orders Signal Shift in AI Policy](https://www.kslaw.com/news-and-insights/trump-administration-early-executive-orders-signal-shift-in-ai-policy)]. This creates uncertainty about the current federal regulatory landscape.

### Implementation Timeline Uncertainties
- The timeline and scope of US federal preemption of state AI laws remains uncertain despite policy framework announcements
- EU AI Act implementation details are still developing, with codes of practice pending for specific technical requirements

## Knowledge Gaps

### Technical Implementation Details
- Specific technical requirements for GPAI model documentation under the EU AI Act remain unclear pending the development of codes of practice
- Practical implementation mechanisms for EU AI Act GPAI obligations are still being developed by regulatory authorities

### US Policy Development
- The scope and timeline for comprehensive federal AI legislation in the US remains undefined
- The relationship between federal voluntary frameworks and emerging state-level mandatory requirements is unclear
- Enforcement mechanisms for any future federal AI requirements have not been established

# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary

The EU AI Act establishes mandatory conformity assessment procedures for high-risk AI systems before market placement or service deployment. The framework includes two primary assessment routes: internal control (self-assessment) and third-party assessment involving notified bodies. While the legal framework is established, the operational infrastructure remains incomplete, with Member States required to designate notifying authorities by August 2, 2025, but no specific notified bodies publicly designated yet.

## Key Findings

### Mandatory Conformity Assessment Requirements

**Core Obligation** (Confidence: 85%)
High-risk AI systems require conformity assessment procedures before being placed on the market or put into service. [Article 43: Conformity Assessment | EU Artificial Intelligence Act](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/43/)

**Dual Assessment Framework** (Confidence: 75%)
There are two main conformity assessment procedures: internal control (self-assessment) and third-party assessment involving notified bodies. [Conformity Assessments under the EU AI Act: A step-by step guide](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)

### Third-Party Assessment Procedures

**Notified Body Assessment Process** (Confidence: 85%)
Third-party conformity assessment (Annex VII) involves assessment of quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body. [Annex VII: Conformity Based on Assessment of the Quality](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/annex/7/)

**Harmonized Legislation Requirements** (Confidence: 85%)
For high-risk AI systems covered by Union harmonisation legislation in Annex I, providers must follow the relevant conformity assessment procedure required under those legal acts. [Article 43: Conformity Assessment | EU Artificial Intelligence Act](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/43/)

**Special Sector Requirements** (Confidence: 80%)
High-risk AI systems intended for law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities require specific notified body procedures. [Article 43: Conformity Assessment | EU Artificial Intelligence Act](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/43/)

### Notified Body Infrastructure and Designation

**Member State Designation Deadline** (Confidence: 85%)
Member States must designate notifying authorities responsible for assessment, designation and notification of conformity assessment bodies by August 2, 2025. [Tasks in 2024-2025 - EU AI Act](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/FLI-Tasks-Member-States-2024-25.pdf)

**Application Requirements** (Confidence: 85%)
Conformity assessment bodies must submit applications to notifying authorities including description of activities, modules, and AI system types they claim competence for. [Article 29: Application of a Conformity Assessment Body](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/29/)

**Commission Registry** (Confidence: 85%)
The European Commission will maintain a publicly available list of notified bodies with their identification numbers and activities. [Article 35: Identification Numbers and Lists of Notified Bodies](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/35/)

**EDPS Designation** (Confidence: 70%)
The European Data Protection Supervisor (EDPS) has been designated as a notified body for conformity assessments of certain high-risk AI systems used by EU institutions. [EU AI Act - Updates, Compliance, Training](https://www.artificial-intelligence-act.com/)

### Compliance Outcomes

**CE Marking Requirement** (Confidence: 80%)
High-risk AI systems that pass conformity assessment must bear CE marking and receive EU technical documentation assessment certificate. [Article 48: CE Marking | EU Artificial Intelligence Act](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/48/)

## Contradictions & Uncertainties

No direct contradictions were identified in the extracted claims. However, several uncertainties exist regarding implementation details and operational readiness.

## Knowledge Gaps

### Critical Implementation Gaps

1. **Notified Body Availability**: No specific notified bodies have been publicly designated yet - the Commission's list referenced in Article 35 is not available in current sources.

2. **Operational Timeline Uncertainty**: Timeline unclear for when notified bodies will be operational relative to August 2026 high-risk AI obligations start date.

3. **Assessment Route Determination**: Specific criteria for when third-party vs self-assessment is required not fully detailed in sources.

4. **Technical Standards**: Details on harmonised standards referenced in conformity assessment procedures not provided in available sources.

### Compliance Planning Implications

The gap between the August 2025 notifying authority designation deadline and the August 2026 high-risk AI system compliance deadline creates uncertainty for organizations planning conformity assessments requiring notified body involvement.
